system_overview: This specification solves a combinatorial puzzle from the U.S. radio program Car Talk (22 October 2011 episode). The problem: a farmer has an N-pound stone and a balance scale. How can he break the stone into P pieces so that, using those pieces and the balance scale, he can weigh out any integral number of pounds from 1 through N? The specification is generalized to arbitrary N and P, and computes all solutions by exhaustive enumeration.
actors_and_components: There are no concurrent actors. The specification defines constant operators that enumerate all valid ways to break a stone and test which breaks constitute valid solutions. The key components are: a recursive summation operator over finite sets, a definition of all valid breaks (ways to partition the stone into P integer-weight pieces), a representation checker (whether a given weight can be balanced using subsets of the pieces on each side of the scale), and a solution checker.
state_variables: There are no state variables. This is a purely constant-level specification with no state machine or transitions. All definitions are constant operators and sets.
initial_state: NOT_SPECIFIED — there is no state machine.
actions: NOT_SPECIFIED — there is no state machine. The specification defines the following computations: (1) A break is a function from piece indices (1 through P) to weights (1 through N) such that the weights sum to N and are in non-decreasing order (to avoid counting permutations of the same partition). (2) A representation of weight w using break B consists of two disjoint subsets S and T of piece indices such that w plus the total weight of pieces in S equals the total weight of pieces in T (S goes on the corn side, T on the opposite side of the balance). (3) A break is a solution if every weight from 1 through N has a valid representation. (4) The set of all solutions is computed by filtering all breaks through the solution predicate. (5) An expanded solution display is provided that shows, for each weight, which pieces go on each side of the balance.
safety_properties: NOT_SPECIFIED — there is no state machine.
liveness_properties: NOT_SPECIFIED — there is no state machine.
model_bounds: N (total stone weight) and P (number of pieces) are declared as constants. For the original puzzle, N = 40 and P = 4. The unique solution for these values breaks the stone into pieces of weights 1, 3, 9, and 27 (powers of 3).
additional_assumptions: The specification is designed for constant evaluation by a model checker rather than for state-space exploration. The expanded solutions display assumes all piece weights are distinct.
